_howto: Arm angles are in degrees: 0 = straight out to the right, 90 = straight up, -90 = straight down, 180 = straight out to the left. a = the ref's pointing arm (pink), b = the other arm. extra adds a prop: card, flag, ball, wave, arc, open, neck.
officialNote: These pictures are simple guides. [HANNAH: check each one against the official World Rugby signals before launch]

signals.name: Penalty
signals.desc: Arm angled up, pointing to the team that gets the penalty.

signals.name: Free kick
signals.desc: Arm bent at a right angle: upper arm level, forearm straight up, toward the team that gets the free kick.

signals.name: Advantage
signals.desc: Arm held out at waist height toward the team that has the advantage. Keep playing!

signals.name: Knock-on
signals.desc: Arm up above the head with an open hand, moved back and forth.

signals.name: Forward pass
signals.desc: Hands make a passing motion forward.

signals.name: Try
signals.desc: Arm raised straight up, with the ref's back to the dead ball line.

signals.name: Offside (ruck, maul, scrum, lineout)
signals.desc: Arm hanging straight down, swung along the offside line.

signals.name: Tackler not releasing
signals.desc: Arms brought together as if grabbing a player, then opened as if letting go.

signals.name: Not releasing the ball (holding on)
signals.desc: Both hands held close to the chest, as if hugging a ball.

signals.name: High tackle
signals.desc: Hand moved flat across the front of the neck.

signals.name: Scrum
signals.desc: Arm held level, pointing to the team that gets the put in.

signals.name: Lineout (touch)
signals.desc: The assistant referee raises their flag, then points to the team that throws in.

signals.name: Yellow card
signals.desc: Ref holds up a yellow card. The player goes to the sin bin for 10 minutes.

signals.name: Obstruction
signals.desc: Arms crossed in front of the chest.
